title: Daily Hustle
medium: Acrylic on digital print, mounted on board (mixed media)
description: In Daily Hustle, Enifome gives the burden greater prominence than the men carrying it. A towering mass of pale bundles dominates the composition, while the labourers merge into dark, fragmented forms against a restless landscape of blue and burning orange. Through semi-abstraction, layered colour and disrupted outlines, he shifts attention from individual identity to collective effort. The imbalance is deliberate in its visual effect: the goods command attention, while those responsible for moving them are almost lost beneath their weight. What emerges is a portrait of everyday survival, where strength is measured not by what is seen, but by what must be endured. PROVENANCE & AUTHENTICITY Artist's Collection | Ozuwo Enifome, Nigeria. Original artwork. Signed Certificate of Authenticity provided upon sale. EXHIBITION HISTORY2024 -- October Rain: 17th Annual Juried Art Exhibition, Society of Nigerian Artists (SNA), Tim & Carol Gallery of Art, GRA Ikeja, Lagos, Nigeria. 12 November 2024.Digitopainting.

title: The Durbar Drummers
medium: Acrylic on digital print, mounted on board (mixed media)
description: The Durbar Drummers turns a gathering of performers into a composition that seems to move to its own beat. Rounded drums punctuate a close formation of dark figures, while passages of red rise through layered greens and earthy tones. Enifome resists the neat separation of musician from audience: broken contours and repeated marks allow one body to merge with the next. The arrangement creates the sensation of rhythm travelling through a crowd rather than belonging to a single performer. In this painting, drumming is not simply an event to be witnessed; it becomes a shared energy that holds the gathering together. PROVENANCE & AUTHENTICITY Artist's Collection | Ozuwo Enifome, Nigeria. Original artwork. Signed Certificate of Authenticity provided upon sale.

title: Durbar
medium: Acrylic on digital print, mounted on board (mixed media)
description: Durbar places the viewer almost within the ceremonial procession. Horses, riders and upright staffs press towards the picture plane, while the pale, textured background offers little escape from their commanding presence. Rather than rendering every detail with documentary precision, Enifome lets decorated forms collide and dissolve into vigorous surface marks. This compressed arrangement suggests the spectacle, pride and intensity of the occasion without reducing it to costume or pageantry. The painting draws its force from proximity: we encounter the Durbar not as a distant display of tradition, but as a living event whose scale and authority are felt at close quarters. PROVENANCE & AUTHENTICITY Artist's Collection | Ozuwo Enifome, Nigeria. Original artwork. Signed Certificate of Authenticity provided upon sale.

title: The Street Guitarist
medium: Acrylic on digital print, mounted on board (mixed media)
description: The Street Guitarist is less concerned with a faithful likeness than with the force of a musician's presence. Enifome stretches the figure through a narrow vertical space, breaking its outline with deep greens, reds and flashes of pink. Dense marks interrupt the body and its surroundings, as though the performance has unsettled the image itself. The guitarist is partly concealed, yet the intense colour refuses to let the figure disappear. That tension gives the work its character: a street performance may be fleeting and easily overlooked, but the artist grants this musician the visual insistence of someone determined to be heard. PROVENANCE & AUTHENTICITY Artist's Collection | Ozuwo Enifome, Nigeria. Original artwork. Signed Certificate of Authenticity provided upon sale.

title: Morning Market
medium: Acrylic on digital print, mounted on board (mixed media)
description: Morning Market opens beneath an unusually generous blue sky. Below it, crowded umbrellas form a lively band of pink, yellow and blue, crossed by poles and lines that pull the eye back into the trading ground. Enifome builds the composition on the contrast between spaciousness overhead and the concentrated activity below. Small, repeated marks give the market its restless texture without isolating every stall or trader. The title fixes the scene at the beginning of a day, when work is gathering momentum and possibility has not yet given way to fatigue. Its optimism comes from the colour and light, not from sentiment. PROVENANCE & AUTHENTICITY Artist's Collection | Ozuwo Enifome, Nigeria. Original artwork. Signed Certificate of Authenticity provided upon sale.

title: Daily Chores
medium: Acrylic on digital print, mounted on board (mixed media)
description: In Daily Chores, a bent figure fills the picture with a sweeping dark curve, its posture picked out against strong yellow and ochre. The task itself is barely specified. Enifome directs attention instead to the body's movement, using a heavy silhouetie and nervous surface marks to make a familiar gesture feel consequential. The figure nearly merges with its surroundings, yet the arc of the back remains unmistakable. Unlike the public exertion of Daily Hustle, this painting speaks of labour that happens quietly and repeatedly, otien without witness. The artist gives an ordinary act the gravity usually reserved for a more celebrated subject. PROVENANCE & AUTHENTICITY Artist's Collection | Ozuwo Enifome, Nigeria. Original artwork. Signed Certificate of Authenticity provided upon sale.

title: My Boat and I
medium: Acrylic on digital print, mounted on board (mixed media)
description: My Boat and I rests on a strikingly unequal pairing. The broad, dark green vessel occupies much of the lower picture, while the fisherman appears as a slight upright figure beside it. Above them, Enifome leaves a wide expanse of pale sky, giving their shared space a rare stillness. Fine, restless marks connect boat, shore and figure, preventing either from standing entirely apart. The first-person title suggests more than ownership: this boat is the man's working companion and perhaps the measure of his independence. By making the vessel so visually substantial, Enifome allows an everyday object to carry the weight of a personal relationship. PROVENANCE & AUTHENTICITY Artist's Collection | Ozuwo Enifome, Nigeria. Original artwork. Signed Certificate of Authenticity provided upon sale.

title: Children of Makoko Waterfront
medium: Acrylic on digital print, mounted on board (mixed media)
description: The red boats in Children of Makoko Waterfront push boldly into the foreground, their angled hulls cuting across patches of turquoise and dark water. Behind them, smaller figures gather along a densely worked shore. Enifome uses this shiti in scale to move the eye from the physical presence of the boats to the children whose lives unfold around them. Abraded colour and layered marks keep the waterfront active rather than picturesque. The children are not offered as anonymous symbols of hardship; they belong to a particular inhabited place. The painting's tenderness lies in that sense of belonging, even as the bustling environment commands our attention. PROVENANCE & AUTHENTICITY Artist's Collection | Ozuwo Enifome, Nigeria. Original artwork. Signed Certificate of Authenticity provided upon sale.

title: Hopelessly Hopeful
medium: Acrylic on digital print, mounted on board (mixed media)
description: Hopelessly Hopeful approaches begging through abstraction rather than a literal scene of outstretched hands. Violet and vivid magenta push against a broad field of darkness, while pale, broken contours briefly suggest human figures before losing them again. Enifome withholds the reassurance of clear faces and stable outlines; the viewer must work to recognise the people at the heart of the painting. This choice is central to its title. The figures seem vulnerable to disappearance, yet the fierce colour insists on their presence. Hope here is neither a promise nor an easy consolation. It survives stubbornly within an image shaped by deprivation. PROVENANCE & AUTHENTICITY Artist's Collection | Ozuwo Enifome, Nigeria. Original artwork. Signed Certificate of Authenticity provided upon sale.

title: Ewa Agoyin
medium: Acrylic on digital print, mounted on board (mixed media)
description: Ewa Agoyin centres on the poise of a street vendor carrying her wares above her head. The stacked containers widen dramatically over a slender figure, producing a vertical composition that seems precarious and assured at once. Enifome sets the silhouetie against warm orange architecture, then introduces cooler blue through the clothing and lively marks across the surface. He turns the practical skill of carrying and selling food into the painting's defining formal achievement: balance. The title locates this figure within a recognisable food-trading tradition, while the upright posture gives her a quiet authority. Her work is everyday, but her presence is unmistakable. PROVENANCE & AUTHENTICITY Artist's Collection | Ozuwo Enifome, Nigeria. Original artwork. Signed Certificate of Authenticity provided upon sale.

title: Gender Discussions
medium: Acrylic on digital print, mounted on board (mixed media)
description: Gender Discussions gathers several figures inside a dark, compressed space, where red gestures and scatiered illuminated faces are easier to distinguish than individual bodies. Enifome declines to give the viewer one clear speaker or a settled point of view. Instead, he uses overlapping silhoueties and interrupted patches of colour to suggest a conversation shaped by competing voices. The narrow opening of blue above the group offers a counterpoint to the intensity below, but does not resolve it. The title invites us to consider the difficulty of speaking and being heard across difference. What matiers is not a declared winner, but the charged space between the participants. PROVENANCE & AUTHENTICITY Artist's Collection | Ozuwo Enifome, Nigeria. Original artwork. Signed Certificate of Authenticity provided upon sale.
